decisions.reason: Removing the call-to-action requirement does not change the selected product benefits, claims, or source materials.
The required keywords and wording constraints remain valid independently of whether the video includes a call to action.
Removing the call to action does not alter the Hindi-only language requirement for the remaining script and dialogue.
The target market and audience age range are independent of the removed call-to-action behavior.
The source does not change which reference video should guide the creative or how it should be adapted.
The opening-hook requirements remain independently applicable and are not logically changed by removal of the closing call to action.
The call-to-action removal does not resolve or modify the required audio level or advertising mix standard.
The source does not modify the requested preview duration, content, language, or approval purpose.
Professional mobile-optimized subtitles remain a separate post-production requirement unaffected by the call-to-action removal.
The source does not change the nationality or gender preference for actors.
The required realistic native-looking UGC visual style remains valid independently of the call-to-action requirement.
Both products can still appear together, including in a closing shot, without an organic call to action.
